fields.label: Read windows and application text
fields.help: Read window metadata and accessible text. No per-window approval.

fields.label: View desktop images
fields.help: Allow requested images and the selected automatic perception mode.

fields.label: Read local files
fields.help: Read any local file your Windows account can read, including private documents.

fields.label: Interact with applications
fields.help: Use supported application controls; file authoring is delegated.

fields.label: Control the 3D companion
fields.help: Allow companion poses, movement and presentation.

fields.label: Delegate to specialist agents
fields.help: Allow tasks to be dispatched to configured specialist agents.

fields.label: Direct user-file writing (no writer available)
fields.help: Off by default. File authoring goes to specialists. This does not install a writer.

fields.label: Enable voice features
fields.help: Make voice available. Start the microphone separately in the voice interface.

fields.label: Automatic perception mode
fields.help: native-only adds no automatic images; image-on-prompt attaches a reduced image of the whole desktop (every monitor) to each message, and SORA can look closer at one window; adaptive interprets changed window images at the configured interval. Images are never recorded.

fields.label: Pause automatic perception
fields.help: Pause automatic metadata and images. Explicit read/look requests remain available under Companion access.

fields.label: Include window metadata on prompts
fields.help: Add fresh window titles and recent application identity, not document bodies. Requires window access.

fields.label: Include Desktop file metadata on prompts
fields.help: Add a bounded Desktop directory preview, not file contents. Requires local-file access.

fields.label: Background refresh interval (seconds)
fields.help: Adaptive only. Minimum time between refreshes; conversation preempts background work. Unchanged window images do not invoke the model again.

fields.label: Background context maximum age (seconds)
fields.help: Adaptive only. Reject background context not reverified within this age. It is interpreted data, never authority for an action.

fields.label: Vision detail
fields.help: How much of each image SORA's model can see. Low, medium and high set the image token budget, physical batch and context length together; changing any of those by hand makes this Custom. Higher detail increases response times and context usage, but SORA reads your screen more reliably and guesses less. Applies when the model reloads.

fields.label: Image token budget (per image)
fields.help: llama.cpp --image-max-tokens: the most tokens one image may use. Set by Vision detail; editing it switches Vision detail to Custom. Physical batch must be at least this.

fields.label: Context length (tokens)
fields.help: llama.cpp --ctx-size. Set by Vision detail, since images use context; editing it switches Vision detail to Custom.

fields.label: Listening
fields.help: press: hold the Chat microphone button to talk. always: the microphone stays open while voice is on, and she answers when you say her name (or keep talking just after she replies). Audio stays in memory on this PC; it is saved only with a moment she chooses to remember, and forgetting that memory deletes it. Start voice again to apply.

fields.label: Names she answers to (always-on listening)
fields.help: Comma-separated names she answers to when listening is always on, for example "sora, zora" if speech recognition sometimes mishears her name.

fields.label: Keep listening after she replies (seconds)
fields.help: After she finishes speaking, you can keep talking without her name for this many seconds. 0 turns it off.

fields.label: Voice to the brain
fields.help: auto: brains that hear audio natively (Gemma 4 E2B and E4B) receive your voice itself, with the transcript as a hint. transcribe: send only the speech-to-text transcript.

fields.label: Decision layer (System-1)
fields.help: A small fast model (Laya, on the GPU) chooses which kinds of tools her brain sees for each message. Fewer choices make a small brain's tool use more reliable. shadow: it decides and the decision is logged for training, but every tool stays available. enforce: only the chosen kinds are offered. off: not used. Needs scripts/setup-decision-layer.ps1.

fields.label: Offer a tool family from this probability
fields.help: Lower offers more tools (fewer missed, more for the brain to choose from); higher offers fewer. Untrained, 0.25 kept every needed kind in testing while offering about half.

fields.label: Decision layer device
fields.help: auto uses the GPU when available (Vulkan on AMD). Applies to the next message.

fields.label: laya runner (blank uses the setup script's)
fields.help: The ggmlc laya runner. Blank: .local/decision from the setup script.

fields.label: Laya model GGUF (blank uses the setup script's)
fields.help: A Laya GGUF compiled by ggmlc (not a llama.cpp model).

fields.label: Memory manager
fields.help: A small embedding model (EmbeddingGemma 2) reads each memory so she can find memories by meaning, link related ones and notice repeats and updates. on (default): her replies see the memories most relevant to your message. shadow: her replies see memories sharing words with your message and your most recent ones, and what meaning-based recall would have chosen is recorded for comparison. off: not used. Needs scripts/setup-memory-embedder.ps1.

fields.label: Memory embedder device
fields.help: gpu uses about 0.2 GB of video memory; cpu is slower but uses none.

fields.label: Embedding server (blank uses the setup script's)
fields.help: llama.cpp b11516 or newer. Blank: .local/llama.cpp-b11516 from the setup script.

fields.label: Embedding model GGUF (blank uses the setup script's)
fields.help: An EmbeddingGemma 2 GGUF. Changing it re-embeds every memory.

fields.label: Avatar model (VRM)
fields.help: The VRM avatar she wears, applied when SORA next starts. Default: Alice, kept in .local\avatars\Alice.vrm (outside git; her licence forbids sharing or editing the file). Credit: Alice (Zenless Zone Zero): original model by miHoYo; VRM by Niko on VRoid Hub. Blank, or a missing file, uses the built-in Seed-san.
